scope: Chronology of surviving RAS-described Hodgson list/inventory objects used for storage, transport, repacking and institutional donation, without assuming direct textual descent among every state.
central_claim: The 1864 India Office donation list belongs to a longer pre-institutional history of box/trunk/store inventories; RAS states that the 1858 store list BHH/11/14 became the 1864 donation list, and a separate printed annotated August 1864 state survives as BHH/19/5.

source_hierarchy: Tier 1: RAS BHH/11/14 handwritten 1858-64 store/donation list; BHH/5/18 2 Aug 1864 draft; BHH/19/5 Aug 1864 printed annotated list
Tier 2: India Office accession, Hall inspection, English/Hindi content lists and institutional manifest copy if located
source_control_rules: Chronological succession does not prove textual descent among all list objects.
RAS's statement that BHH/11/14 store list became donation list is direct catalogue evidence; exact textual changes require page comparison.
Do not assign BHH/19/5 annotations to Hodgson until handwriting/provenance is checked.
Do not equate BHH/11/1 five boxes with BHH/11/3 Trunk No.1 or later 1864 trunks without content reconciliation.
Do not infer that 1858 store order already had the final 1864 version-family co-bundling until BHH/11/14 and BHH/19/5 are compared.
Treat lists as paper objects with their own state, custody and revision histories.
